subject: MindMap AI – hosted API cost targets & peak concurrency check
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@mindmap.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (hosted API)

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and items we promised to put in writing so your procurement and engineering teams can align: 

What you described
- Production launch target: early Q4 (pilot now, full launch ~6–8 weeks).
- Primary use case: document summarization + context-aware suggestions in the editor. Average prompt+response ~1.8k tokens, peaks up to 6k.
- Expected monthly: 22M–36M tokens (conservative to stretch); peak concurrency window: 220–350 TPS for brief spikes during US business hours.

Initial pricing guidance we walked through
- Baseline target: aim for $12–$20 per 1M tokens depending on SLA/peak guarantees and caching.
- Burst/peak handling: recommend a small dedicated burst reservation or soft-burst policy to cover the 10–15 minute spikes.

Action items (next steps)
1) Samir: confirm which of the two volume bands below is closest to your plan and whether the peak estimate is for sustained 10–15 minute windows or very short bursts.
   - Band A (conservative): ~22M tokens/mo, typical TPS 35–60, peaks 220 TPS for short windows.
   - Band B (stretch): ~36M tokens/mo, typical TPS 60–120, peaks 350 TPS.
2) Redwood (Ben + Jordan): we'll attach an updated pricing worksheet with tiered $/1M assumptions, breakout for streaming vs non-streaming calls, and a suggested burst reservation model.
3) Both: target a procurement-ready SOW draft by next Thursday (9/9).

Attaching the draft pricing sheet and an SOW skeleton for review. If the token estimate above is off by more than ±20%, call it out — that materially affects recommended slab pricing and the suggested burst size.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-draft-MindMap-2026.pdf (SOW skeleton)
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@mindmap.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Anand <priya@mindmap.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (hosted API)

Evelyn — really appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with Priya and the infra lead: 

Numbers adjustments
- Monthly tokens: the 22M–36M is accurate for text generation traffic, but we also expect ~4M embedding tokens (search/indexing) per month. For pricing purposes, embeddings can be treated at the lower unit-rate, but want that called out.
- Peak description: the 220–350 TPS windows are short spikes tied to promo campaigns (2–12 minutes), not sustained for hours. Sustained normal peak is closer to ~60–80 TPS.

Budget and target $/1M
- Procurement range: $8k–$16k per month total committed spend depending on SLA. That maps roughly to ~$9–$18 per 1M tokens for our higher-latency non-streaming paths; if you can offer a favorable streaming rate or a bundled burst credit, we can skew to the higher band.

Requirements that affect pricing
- We need predictable latency under 500ms p95 for streaming in the editor path; that will push toward a reserved burst or soft pre-warming.
- SOC2 evidence + simple flow for audit logs retention (we'll ask security questionnaire soon).

We approve the SOW skeleton in principle — please include an embedding line-item and explicit burst handling (credits vs reserved capacity) in the next draft.

Thanks — Samir
CTO, MindMap AI

On Thu, Sep 2, 2026 at 3:08 PM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier....
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MindMap pricing inputs — suggested framing

Eve — quick internal note before we send the SOW: based on Samir's clarification, propose we structure the pricing sheet like this: 

1) Two-line committed slab (text gen):
   - 20M/mo committed: $10 per 1M tokens (baseline)
   - 35M/mo committed: $8.5 per 1M tokens (volume discount)
2) Embeddings: separate band at $3.50 per 1M embeddings
3) Streaming (editor path): +20% on top of text gen unit unless they commit to a burst reservation (makes pre-warm cost predictable)
4) Burst handling: offer both options — (A) 1-hour burst pool credits (consumable) priced as a fixed monthly add-on, (B) temporary reserved capacity priced by peak TPS window (recommended for their 2–12 minute spikes)
5) SLA uplift: p95 latency target 500ms for streaming available as a paid uplift (we can make lower $/1M if they accept a soft-fallback policy for rare overloads)

Ben suggests we lead with the 20M/$10 & 35M/$8.5 positions in the SOW and show sensitivity to peak-handling cost. Also recommend a short note calling out that if embeddings exceed 10% of gen tokens, we revisit unit economics.

If that works I’ll update redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx and add a one-page pricing summary to the SOW.

— Ben
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@mindmap.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Priya Anand <priya@mindmap.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2026 10:43:00 -0700
Subject: Final SOW & pricing worksheet — draft for procurement

Samir / Priya — attached is the updated SOW skeleton and a concise pricing summary that reflects Ben's recommended framing. Highlights: 
- Committed slabs: 20M @ $10/1M, 35M @ $8.5/1M (text gen)
- Embeddings: $3.50/1M (separate item)
- Streaming: +20% unless a burst reservation is purchased (we show both options)
- Burst: example pricing for a 300 TPS 10-minute reserve vs a monthly burst credit pack — both models priced so procurement can compare CIP.

Next steps: 
1) MindMap to confirm whether they prefer the 20M or 35M slab by EOD Friday (9/12).
2) Redwood to produce a procurement-ready SOW (with DocuSign-ready signature block) by 9/16 if they pick a slab.
3) Security questionnaire to be routed to Security team — Evelyn will send that separately; Samir, Priya, expect a short form + attachments request.

If this aligns, we can also spin up a short 30-minute follow-up to walk procurement through the burst comparison. I’m available Thursday afternoon PST.

Best — Evelyn
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx, SOW-draft-MindMap-2026.pdf
